name: Creative & Media
summary: Image and music generation are mainstream, Chinese labs top video rankings after Sora's exit, and the fight over training data is moving from lawsuits to settlements, licences and labelling rules.

regions.name: Image & design
regions.summary: Image generation is built into chat apps, search and pro tools; Adobe is adding an agent across Creative Cloud, while nonconsensual sexualized images draw regulator action.

landmarks.name: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image)
landmarks.summary: Google released its faster image model on 26 February with output up to 4K; it replaced Nano Banana Pro in the Gemini app and is coming to Search AI Mode and Lens.

landmarks.name: Adobe Firefly AI Assistant
landmarks.summary: Adobe unveiled an agentic assistant on 15 April that runs multi-step tasks across Photoshop, Premiere, Lightroom, Illustrator and other apps from one chat interface.

landmarks.name: Grok sexualized deepfake scandal
landmarks.summary: Grok on X produced undressed images of real people, including children; Ofcom opened a formal probe on 12 January, the EU followed, and Indonesia and Malaysia blocked it.

regions.whyItMatters: Image tools are where most people first meet generative AI, and where misuse against real people is most visible.
regions.openQuestion: Can safeguards and labelling keep pace with models that edit photos of real people on request?

regions.name: Video & film
regions.summary: Chinese labs such as Alibaba, MiniMax and ByteDance top public video rankings after OpenAI shut Sora; studios use AI for effects shots while character licensing remains unsettled.

landmarks.name: OpenAI discontinues Sora
landmarks.summary: OpenAI said on 24 March it would discontinue Sora in the consumer app and API, citing compute demand and a shift to world-simulation research. The app closed on 26 April.
landmarks.note: App closure date (26 April) is from Wikipedia citing OpenAI's help page, not the CBS report

landmarks.name: Disney and OpenAI $1B licensing deal
landmarks.summary: Disney agreed to license 200+ characters to Sora for three years and invest $1B in OpenAI; Deadline reported the deal was never finalized and ended when Sora was shut.
landmarks.note: Announcement confirmed on source page; the collapse is from Deadline, 24 March 2026

landmarks.name: Kling 3.0 launch
landmarks.summary: Kuaishou launched Kling Video 3.0 and 3.0 Omni with clips of up to 15 seconds and native audio in several languages, first for Ultra subscribers.

landmarks.name: Netflix uses generative AI in final footage
landmarks.summary: Netflix said 'The Eternaut' used generative AI for a building-collapse scene, its first use in final footage, finished about ten times faster than usual.

regions.whyItMatters: Video is the costliest media to generate, so it shows whether consumer generative AI can pay for its own compute.
regions.openQuestion: Will studios license characters and libraries to video models, or keep the tools in-house for effects work?

regions.name: Music & audio
regions.summary: Major labels have moved from suing AI music generators to licensing them, a German court has ruled against Suno, and AI tracks now make up half of uploads on one streaming service.

landmarks.name: Warner Music settles with Suno
landmarks.summary: WMG settled its suit and signed a licensing deal; Suno said licensed models would launch in 2026, current models would be deprecated and downloads would need a paid account.

landmarks.name: Universal settles with Udio
landmarks.summary: UMG settled and agreed a licensed, subscription AI music platform with Udio for 2026; until then Udio creations stay inside a walled garden.

landmarks.name: AI tracks pass half of Deezer uploads
landmarks.summary: Deezer said AI-generated tracks passed 50% of daily uploads at peak in June, about 90,000 a day, yet draw only 1 to 3% of streams; it will take down those used for fraud.

landmarks.name: German court rules for GEMA against Suno
landmarks.summary: Munich Regional Court I largely sided with collecting society GEMA, finding Suno's model stored protected songs and reproduced them in outputs. The ruling is not yet final.

regions.whyItMatters: Music is the first creative sector where rights holders and AI generators have moved from court to licensed products.
regions.openQuestion: Will licensed AI music pay artists meaningfully, and can streaming services contain the flood of uploads?

deepDives.why: Collecting societies' estimate of generative AI's economic impact on music and film creators

deepDives.why: Trade publication that follows label licensing deals and AI lawsuits closely

regions.name: Writing & publishing
regions.summary: AI-written books fill self-publishing platforms and dilute revenue per title, while publishers test licensing and authors win payouts over pirated training data.

landmarks.name: Anthropic $1.5B authors settlement approved
landmarks.summary: A US judge gave final approval on 20 July to the largest US copyright settlement: about $3,000 per eligible work, for a class of over 500,000 authors and publishers.

landmarks.name: AI books reach 20% of Amazon self-publishing
landmarks.summary: Preprint on 14,419 self-published genre-fiction e-books finds 20% have substantial AI text but earn a smaller share of sales; revenue per selling book fell in most genres.

landmarks.name: HarperCollins AI training licence
landmarks.summary: HarperCollins offered nonfiction backlist authors $2,500 per title for a three-year opt-in AI training licence; Bloomberg reported the buyer was Microsoft.

regions.whyItMatters: Books are the clearest test of what training data is worth and of how cheap AI text changes a market for human work.
regions.openQuestion: Will per-book licensing become standard, and can platforms stop AI titles from diluting author income?

deepDives.title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books

deepDives.why: A respected publishing analyst on who holds AI rights and how deals are structured

deepDives.title: Publishers Weekly: An AI Licensing Primer for Book Publishers
deepDives.why: Trade-press explainer on how book licensing deals with AI firms work

regions.name: Games & interactive
regions.summary: About half of new Steam games now disclose generative AI, mostly small titles; world models generate explorable scenes but remain research prototypes.

landmarks.name: Google Project Genie
landmarks.summary: Experimental prototype built on the Genie 3 world model lets US Google AI Ultra subscribers generate and explore worlds from text or image prompts.

landmarks.name: Steam rewrites AI disclosure rules
landmarks.summary: Valve reworded its disclosure form to focus on AI-generated content that players see, not efficiency tools used behind the scenes in development.

landmarks.name: Nearly half of new Steam games disclose AI
landmarks.summary: A Reddit user's analysis of about 63,600 games found 49.9% of October 2026 Steam releases disclosed AI content, up from 26.4% a year earlier, more often small titles.

landmarks.name: SAG-AFTRA game deal with AI consent rules
landmarks.summary: Members ratified the Interactive Media Agreement with 95% in favour, ending a 320-day video game strike; it requires disclosure and written consent for AI replicas.

regions.whyItMatters: Games combine art, code, voice and live interaction, so they show how AI spreads through a whole production pipeline.
regions.openQuestion: Will players accept AI-made content in major releases, or will it stay concentrated in small titles?

regions.name: Creators, licensing & provenance
regions.summary: Courts are drawing narrow lines on training and fair use, EU labelling duties began applying in August 2026, and settlements and licensing deals are becoming the norm.

landmarks.name: Getty v Stability AI UK ruling
landmarks.summary: UK High Court rejected Getty's secondary copyright claim, finding Stable Diffusion holds no infringing copies; Getty won only narrow watermark trade mark points.
landmarks.note: Leave to appeal the secondary infringement point was granted in Dec 2025; outcome not confirmed

landmarks.name: EU code on labelling AI-generated content
landmarks.summary: The Commission published the final voluntary code on marking and labelling AI content; Article 50 duties apply from 2 August 2026, with older systems given until 2 December.
landmarks.note: Grace period to 2 Dec 2026 for existing systems is per artificialintelligenceact.eu timeline

landmarks.name: Thomson Reuters v Ross upheld on appeal
landmarks.summary: Third Circuit held on 29 September that training a legal search tool on Westlaw headnotes was not fair use, while leaving the question open for generative models.

regions.whyItMatters: How courts and regulators treat training data and labelling sets the terms on which every generative model is built and sold.
regions.openQuestion: Is training generative models on copyrighted work fair use, and who gets paid if it is not?
